solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist heading for shops, getting French bread

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of shops
bread is slang for money, and argent is the French word for money (and silver)

explanation.surface: A painter popping into the shops and picking up a baguette on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French bread' looks like a baguette, but bread is slang for money, which in French is argent. John Singer Sargent was a portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was a celebrated American portrait painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Tribal group determined to seize power

indicators.note: seizing grabs hold of something, so the first word clasps the second within it

blocks.note: set on something means determined to do it
P is the abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A tribe resolved to take control of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A sept is a clan or branch of a family, especially in Ireland or Scotland, so a kinship group.

clue.text: Complain about resistance one’s seen on line

blocks.note: to rail against something is to protest bitterly
ca is short for circa, meaning about
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone moaning about pushback they have met online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On line' suggests the internet, but the line is a railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: A railcar is a self-propelled railway carriage, a vehicle you would spot running along a track.

clue.text: Eschew restaurants cooking without rind?

indicators.note: the rind is the outer skin, so taking it away strips the outermost letters off each end

blocks.note: heating food is cooking it

explanation.surface: A recipe for cooking cheese without its rind, and a diner avoiding restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rind' suggests cheese or bacon, but it means the outside letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to have a meal at home rather than going out, so it means avoiding dining out.

clue.text: Some paper by whizz going over economic shortfall

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means flipping upwards, so the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a page is a single sheet of paper
to dart is to dash or whizz along

explanation.surface: A paper written by a genius reviewing a financial deficit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whizz' reads as an expert, but it is the verb to speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is the amount by which a country's imports exceed its exports, a deficit in its national accounts.

clue.text: Cheer up tot in depressed area

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other, as a thing sits within its surroundings

blocks.note: a glen is a narrow valley, a low-lying area
to tot up is to add up a sum

explanation.surface: Trying to brighten the mood of a small child living in a deprived neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' reads as a toddler but is the verb to tot, meaning to add. A glen, a narrow valley, is the depressed area.
explanation.definitionFit: To gladden someone is to make them happier, which is exactly what cheering them up means.

clue.text: Become active, ultimately subsisting on fruit

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept
in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second

blocks.note: the last letter of subsisting
the olive is botanically a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone who ends up living off fruit alone and feels energised.
explanation.definitionFit: When a system or website goes live it starts operating for real, so it becomes active.

clue.text: Workers caught in completely outrageous plot

indicators.note: something caught in a trap is held inside it, so the first word goes within another

blocks.note: all means wholly, as in 'all alone'
OTT is short for over the top
workers are often men in crosswords

explanation.surface: Labourers implicated in a thoroughly scandalous conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' sounds like a conspiracy; it is a patch of land. In Britain an allotment is a rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small piece of ground rented for growing vegetables, so it is a garden plot.

clue.text: Fighter stops old Chinese leader giving people a hand

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so the first word is pushed inside the next as a bung

blocks.note: Deng Xiaoping led China from 1978 to 1989
Muhammad Ali, the boxer

explanation.surface: A boxer halting an elderly Chinese ruler who was offering help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giving people a hand' sounds like helping; it is handing out cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing in card games means distributing cards, so each player receives a hand from the dealer.

clue.text: New area for sufferers, drinking anaesthetic down

indicators.note: drinking takes liquid inside, so the outer letters swallow another word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for new
a hospital ward holds patients
ether was an early general anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A fresh hospital ward where patients are dosed with anaesthetic.
explanation.walkthrough: The anaesthetic goes in between the two pieces that start the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Netherward is an old word meaning towards the lower regions, so it means downwards.

clue.text: Long to host current party game

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the first word holds the next one inside it

blocks.note: to pant for something is to long for it
I is the symbol for electric current
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: Desperate to stage a party with a games theme for the current crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' is a verb here, to pant after something, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintball is a combat sport in which players shoot one another with dye pellets, so it is a type of game.

clue.text: Most insignificant article to stuff in case

indicators.note: stuffing a thing in means pushing it inside something else, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: lest means in case, as in 'lest we forget'
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: The smallest item to pack into a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like luggage, but 'in case' is the connective lest, and 'in' belongs to the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Least is the superlative of little, describing whatever matters or counts for the smallest amount.

clue.text: Terrible overreactions in the players’ training area

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the following letters are wrecked and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written, all thirteen letters used

explanation.surface: Footballers throwing tantrums on the training ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' suggests a sports team, but they are musicians, and their training area is a music college.
explanation.definitionFit: A conservatoire is a college where musicians, who are players of instruments, receive their training.

clue.text: Welcoming crossing ring road that’s not too steep

indicators.note: something crossing a path is set across it, so the later pieces are laid inside the first word

blocks.note: affable means friendly and approachable
O is ring-shaped
Rd is the abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: A friendly ring road with only gentle gradients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like a slope, but it is informal for overpriced.
explanation.definitionFit: Affordable means reasonably priced, and steep is an informal word for excessively expensive.

clue.text: After warning, put up with distant relative

indicators.note: after tells us the next part follows on directly behind the earlier one

blocks.note: fore is the golfer's shouted warning
to bear something is to tolerate it

explanation.surface: Having been told off, someone resigns themselves to tolerating a far-flung cousin.
explanation.walkthrough: Fore! is shouted on a golf course to warn people a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is an ancestor, a family member separated from you by many generations.

clue.text: Plant experts in NATO? Its buildings in need of emptying out

indicators.note: emptying removes the contents, so only the outside letters of the word stay
out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the outside letters of buildings

explanation.surface: Questioning whether the alliance's bases want clearing out by plant specialists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests factories next to buildings, but it means flora.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists are scientists who study plants, so they are specialists in plant life.

clue.text: Return of comic with, say, novelty

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so everything that follows is read from right to left

blocks.note: a wag is a joker
W is the abbreviation for with
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: A comedian coming back with a new act.
explanation.definitionFit: A gewgaw is a showy trinket, the kind of cheap little item sold as a novelty.

clue.text: Refuses to patronise children around bed time

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word encloses the ones after it

blocks.note: boys are male children
a cot is a small bed
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Children who will not go along with bedtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Patronise' means to be a customer of, not to talk down to.
explanation.definitionFit: To boycott a shop or company is to refuse to buy from it, deliberately withholding custom as a protest.

clue.text: Take too much vermouth during day periodically? This is rum

indicators.note: during means within a span of time, so one piece sits inside another
periodically means at regular intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: OD is short for overdose
the first of the alternate letters of day
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
the other alternate letter of day

explanation.surface: Drinking too much vermouth in the daytime now and then is a strange habit.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum is not the drink but the British adjective for odd; 'This is rum' points at the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang rum means strange, and an oddity is something strange, so it is what is rum.

clue.text: Woman who’s experienced desire over clothes

indicators.note: to clothe something is to wrap it up, so the second word surrounds the first

blocks.note: done means finished, over
a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A seasoned woman whose passion runs to clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothes' looks like a noun, garments, but it is the verb to clothe, to cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most senior or respected woman in a field, someone with long experience.

clue.text: More stout and ale, drinking large one

indicators.note: something drinking takes liquid into itself, so the outer word swallows the inner pieces

blocks.note: porter is a dark ale
L is the abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A pub order of stout and ale, plus one large drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like the beer but is the adjective meaning portly.
explanation.definitionFit: Portly means stout or heavily built, so its comparative form portlier means more heavily built.

clue.text: People very shortly getting astride horse

indicators.note: a rider astride sits with legs either side, so the phrase straddles the other piece

blocks.note: in a bit means soon
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A person about to climb onto a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People' looks like a noun but is the verb, to populate.
explanation.definitionFit: To people a place is to fill it with inhabitants, so it means the same as to populate or live in it.

clue.text: Sacking crony, create friction the wrong way

indicators.note: the wrong way means facing backwards, so the letters before it run in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
to rub is to cause friction

explanation.surface: Firing a friend and causing ill feeling all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sacking' sounds like a dismissal; it is the coarse fabric sacks are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Burlap is coarse hessian cloth used for making sacks, so it is a kind of sacking material.

clue.text: Stopping speaking, Conservative reluctant to give aid for domestic workers

blocks.note: an actor drying up forgets lines and stops talking
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
loth is a variant spelling of loath, unwilling

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied Tory politician unwilling to fund help for household staff.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, drying up is also the chore of wiping washed dishes, the job the cloth does.
explanation.definitionFit: A drying-up cloth is a tea towel, the fabric used to wipe dishes dry in a household kitchen.

clue.text: Work by Schiller perhaps staged in ancient theatre

blocks.note: Schiller wrote the Ode to Joy, set by Beethoven
a play that is staged is on

explanation.surface: A Schiller drama being performed in an amphitheatre.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain Odeon is a cinema chain, but the original was a Greek concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: An odeon was a building in ancient Greece or Rome for music and poetry performances.

clue.text: Russian king court occasionally expelled

indicators.note: throwing out letters now and then means every other one goes, leaving the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A tsar whose courtiers are banished from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian king' looks like the definition; only 'Russian' is, and 'king' is part of the letter string.
explanation.definitionFit: Igor is a common Russian forename, so a man so named is an example of a Russian.

clue.text: Bishop with responsibility to provide blessing

indicators.note: with means accompanied by, so the next piece is set alongside the first

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
an onus is a duty or burden

explanation.surface: A bishop whose duties include giving the blessing at a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessing' sounds ecclesiastical next to bishop, but it means a welcome extra.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an unexpected advantage or extra benefit, which is what a blessing means in everyday speech.

clue.text: Spooner’s freezing ear is a nuisance in the street

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of neighbouring words

blocks.note: bitter cold is freezing; it takes the opening sound of the next word
lug is British slang for the ear; it takes the opening sound of the previous word

explanation.surface: Someone with a frostbitten ear grumbling in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Lug, or lughole, is British slang for an ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A litterbug drops rubbish in public places, making them a nuisance to everyone else using the street.

clue.text: After son moves back, fizzy drink settles

indicators.note: moving back shifts a letter further along the word, so it is taken out and set down later inside

blocks.note: 7 Up is a brand of lemonade
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Once the boy has stepped away, the fizzy drink in the glass goes flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The S at the front of the drink's name is lifted out and dropped back between its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up a score or account is to make it balanced, which is one sense of settling it.

clue.text: What’s penned by Diderot — an essay about lawmaker

indicators.note: what is penned is enclosed, so the letters lie inside the following words
about means turned round, so the enclosed run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the end of Diderot, an, and the start of essay

explanation.surface: A literary critic's look at an essay by the French philosopher Diderot.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an upper legislative house, so a maker of laws.
